results.reasoning: Judged with no server: I drove `node bin/walkdown.js` on throwaway machines from tools/cli-scenarios.mjs (machine(), FIXTURES), never the real home or this repo's blueprints, and judged against the design that is still only proposed on n-0614 (prototype-cli/drafts/lint-old-layout.html, not yet accepted), which the as-built matches line for line. On g2-old-layout `lint --no-checks` exits 0 with exactly one [upgrade] warning each for checkout (four screens) and search, naming storyboard `prototype:` keys, `prototype.root` in spec.yml and `screens/` and `drafts/` under prototype/, and saying `walkdown upgrade --dry-run` then `walkdown upgrade`; billing, on design: keys with a dated version, gets none; `--blueprint checkout` and `--json` agree. A dry run leaves the warnings; after a real `walkdown upgrade` lint reads 0 warnings on all three. Breaking it: `proposal:` keys alone are named as such; a `proposals/` folder under a design.root is named; a blueprint with seven old screens carrying both keys and all three folders still gets one warning listing every kind; a design.root blueprint with no old keys or folders, and a blueprint with neither key nor designs/, get none. One edge stands outside the steps: a 0.5.0 blueprint whose screen id is literally `drafts`, `screens` or `proposals` has that screen's folder read as an old one, gets the warning, and `walkdown upgrade` says nothing to upgrade, so it never clears (estimated 10-15%: a drafts screen is common in mail, blog and CMS apps; it costs a permanent false warning, not a wrong exit), reported to the dispatching agent rather than filed.
